general_centered_strip_lemma.statement: For bounded A⊂R^m, diam(A)<=1, 0∈A, there are m-1 orthonormal u_1,...,u_{m-1} such that |<u_i,x>|<=1/2 for all x∈A.
general_centered_strip_lemma.proof: For any subspace W of dimension at least 2, the support functions a(u)=sup_A<u,x> and b(u)=sup_A<-u,x> are continuous on S(W), nonnegative, and a(u)+b(u)<=1. The odd continuous function a-b has a zero on connected S(W), yielding a=b<=1/2. Choose such a direction, pass to its orthogonal complement, and iterate until dimension 1 remains.
general_centered_strip_lemma.R6_consequence: applied to the five-dimensional projection, four mutually orthogonal centered unit-width slabs exist

R6_missing_geometric_lemma: Construct a finite five-dimensional truncation/UCS normal system with controlled orbit representatives and, for every resulting R6 lens variant, certify a repartition into at most 32 total pieces of diameter <1 (or show a quantified obstruction for that enlarged template).
conclusion: The R4 method is not dimension-4-only at its algebraic or algorithmic core. The exact bottleneck in R6 is the missing five-dimensional truncation/orbit geometry and its strict-diameter certificate.
